'''Willis Andrew McGahee III''' (born October 21, 1981) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Miami Hurricanes football|Miami Hurricanes]], earning consensus [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors in 2002. McGahee was selected by the [[Buffalo Bills]] in the first round of the [[2003 NFL draft]]. In addition to his time with the Bills, he played for the [[Baltimore Ravens]], [[Denver Broncos]], and [[Cleveland Browns]].

In 2015, McGahee signed on as an athlete for the Miami Surge of the [[National Pro Grid League]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Villa |first=Walter |date=March 9, 2015 |title=Grid's Miami Surge Sign NFL Veteran Willis McGahee |url=https://www.npgl.com/content/posts/grids-miami-surge-sign-nfl-veteran-willis-mcgahee |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150323061118/https://www.npgl.com/content/posts/grids-miami-surge-sign-nfl-veteran-willis-mcgahee |archive-date=March 23, 2015 |website=NPGL.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Dominguez |first=Damect |date=February 10, 2015 |title=The 2015 NPGL Season Looks Bright: Dmitry Klokov, Willis McGahee, New Expansion Teams & More |url=http://boxlifemagazine.com/the-2015-npgl-season-dmitry-klokov-willis-mcgahee-new-expansion-teams-more/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151208133530/http://boxlifemagazine.com/the-2015-npgl-season-dmitry-klokov-willis-mcgahee-new-expansion-teams-more/ |archive-date=December 8, 2015 |access-date=November 13, 2022 |website=BoxLife}}</ref>

'''William Lee McGinest Jr.''' (born December 11, 1971) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]] who played in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for 15 seasons, primarily with the [[New England Patriots]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[USC Trojans football|USC Trojans]], twice receiving first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference football teams|All-Pac-10]] honors, and was selected fourth overall by the Patriots in the [[1994 NFL draft]]. During his 12 seasons with the team, he was named to two [[Pro Bowl]]s and won three [[Super Bowl]] titles. McGinest also holds the postseason record for sacks. For his accomplishments in New England, he was inducted to the [[New England Patriots#New England Patriots Hall of Fame members|Patriots Hall of Fame]] in 2015.

'''Willie Frank Middlebrooks'''<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MiddWi20.htm|title = Willie Middlebrooks Stats|website = [[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref> (born February 12, 1979) is an American former professional [[gridiron football|football]] player who was a [[cornerback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) and [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL).

Middlebrooks was named first-team all-state as a senior at Homestead High School in Homestead, Florida. He played [[college football]] for the [[Minnesota Golden Gophers football|Minnesota Golden Gophers]]. In 1999, he was named Second-Team All-Big Ten. In 2000, he was named First-Team All-Big Ten Conference, but missed the final four games of the season with a fractured ankle. Prior to the 2001 NFL Draft, he was regarded as the best man-coverage player in the Big Ten, with speculation that he would be drafted in the first round, despite his recent injury.

He was the 24th overall pick of the [[Denver Broncos]] in the [[2001 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2001 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2001/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-18 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He began his career with the Broncos, then played for the [[San Francisco 49ers]] before returning to Denver in 2006.

Middlebrooks signed as a free agent with the Argonauts on April 28, 2008.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.argonauts.ca/index.php/roster/show/id/1633|title=Willie Middlebrooks #23 Defensive Back|work=Roster|publisher=Toronto Argonauts Football Club|access-date=2008-06-21|archive-date=2008-06-15|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080615011350/http://argonauts.ca/index.php/roster/show/id/1633|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was named defensive player of Week One of the [[2008 CFL season]] with nine tackles and an interception of a long pass from Winnipeg's [[Kevin Glenn]] near the end of the fourth quarter.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.canada.com/montrealgazette/news/story.html?id=37c1da58-6430-4ad0-835f-48f025b85836|title=Calvillo takes top offensive honours|date=2008-07-03|publisher=Montreal Gazette|access-date=2008-07-04}}</ref>

On June 1, 2011, Middlebrooks announced his retirement after sustaining a serious neck injury he received nearing the end of the 2010 CFL season. <ref>{{cite web|title=Argos' Lemon Unfazed About Having to Compete for Starting Job|url=https://www.tsn.ca/cfl/story/?id=367601|publisher=TSN}}</ref>

'''Willie Thomas Spencer Sr.''' (January 28, 1953 – September 19, 2021) was an American professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL).

Spencer was born in [[Massillon, Ohio]], in 1953. He attended [[Massillon Washington High School]].<ref name=PFA/> In 1971, he led the county with 116 points scored and 1,251 yards.<ref>{{Cite news |date=November 16, 1971 |title=Spencer captures triple crown |work=The Evening Independent |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/62594747/spencer-captures-triple-crown/ |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> He also played basketball and led Jefferson in rebounding as a senior.<ref name=EI72/>

Spencer opted to skip college football and signed in 1972 with the [[Ottawa Rough Riders]] of the [[Canadian Football League]].<ref name="EI72">{{Cite news |date=May 5, 1972 |title=Spencer to try Canadian play |work=The Evening Independent |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/62594801/spencer-to-try-canadian-play/ |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> He was cut by Ottawa in July 1972 and assigned to Indianapolis of the Midwest Football League.<ref>{{Cite news |date=July 14, 1972 |title=Spencer Irked By Demotion |page=B5 |work=The Akron Beacon Journal |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/62594874/spencer-irked/ |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref>

In 1973, he played in the [[Atlantic Coast Football League]] for the [[Hartford Knights]].<ref name=PFA/> He jumped to the [[Memphis Southmen]] of the newly formed [[World Football League]] (WFL) in 1974. He scored five touchdowns against the Jacksonville Sharks on October 2, 1974.<ref>{{Cite news |date=October 3, 1974 |title=Jennings, Spencer Lift Southmen to Easy Win |page=D4 |work=Honolulu Star-Bulletin |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/62594950/jennings-spencer-lift-southmen-to-easy/ |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> He played two seasons with Memphis, appearing in 27 games and rushing for 1,369 yards during the 1974 and 1975 seasons.<ref name="PFA">{{Cite web |title=Willie Spencer |url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/players/spen01800.html |access-date=November 4, 2020 |publisher=Pro Football Archives}}</ref>

The WFL folded after the 1975 season, and Spencer played in 1976 for the [[Minnesota Vikings]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL).<ref name=PFR/> He concluded his football career with the [[New York Giants]] during the 1977 and 1978 seasons. He appeared in a total of 31 NFL games.<ref name="PFR">{{Cite web |title=Willie Spencer |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SpenWi00.htm |access-date=November 2, 2020 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |publisher=Sports Reference LLC}}</ref>

Spencer died on September 19, 2021.<ref>{{cite web |title=Willie Thomas Spencer, Sr. Obituary September 19, 2021 |url=https://www.paquelet.com/obituaries/Willie-Thomas-Spencer-Sr?obId=22443019 |access-date=2025-09-06 |website=Paquelet Funeral Home}}</ref>
